config.title: @keyframes and animation

intro.title: @keyframes and animation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple animated element, like a bouncing ball or a fading box, to bring your web pages to life. You will learn the core concept of defining custom animations using the @keyframes rule, which lets you specify exactly how an element's style changes over time. The main technologies involved are the @keyframes rule to create the animation sequence and the animation property to apply it to an element. By the end, you'll be able to create smooth, eye-catching animations using pure CSS.
intro.usecase: The @keyframes and animation properties are essential for creating smooth, engaging UI feedback and transitions in modern web applications. For example, developers use them to animate loading spinners on dashboards, highlight new notifications with a subtle pulse, or create smooth slide-in effects for modals and side panels. These animations enhance user experience by providing visual cues, guiding attention, and making interfaces feel more responsive and polished. Mastering CSS animations allows you to implement common patterns like progress bars, hover effects on buttons, and attention-grabbing alerts without relying on heavy JavaScript libraries.

objectives: Construct a custom @keyframes rule to define a multi-stage animation sequence.
Apply the animation property to an element to link it to a defined @keyframes rule.
Configure animation duration, timing function, and iteration count to control playback behavior.
Manipulate animation direction and fill-mode to alter the animation's flow and final state.
Integrate multiple animations on a single element by specifying comma-separated values.
Initialize a paused animation and control its playback using the animation-play-state property.
Render a smooth, continuous animation loop using infinite iteration and appropriate timing.

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure to animate
steps.instruction: Create a div element with a class name that will be animated
steps.hint: Add a div element with a class attribute to serve as the target for your animation.
steps.seedCode: /* Add a div element with a class name here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with a class attribute is created, ready to be styled and animated.
successCriteria: A div element with a class attribute is present in the code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a div element with a class attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a div element with a class attribute to serve as the animation target.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the target element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the div element that sets its width to 100px, height to 100px, background-color to blue, and position to relative.
steps.hint: Use a class selector (like .your-class-name) followed by curly braces containing the property declarations.
steps.seedCode:
/* Add a div element with a class name here */

/* Add your CSS rule here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The div element will be visible as a blue square positioned on the page, ready for animation.
successCriteria: The CSS rule includes width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: blue, and position: relative.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include all four properties: width, height, background-color, and position.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling is missing or incorrect. Add a CSS rule that sets width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: blue, and position: relative.

steps.title: Create your first @keyframes rule
steps.instruction: Define a @keyframes rule named 'slide' that moves an element from left: 0px to left: 200px.
steps.hint: Use @keyframes followed by your animation name, then define 'from' and 'to' blocks with the left property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A @keyframes rule named 'slide' is created with from and to states defining left position changes.
successCriteria: The @keyframes rule is named 'slide' and contains both from { left: 0px; } and to { left: 200px; } blocks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your @keyframes rule includes both 'from' and 'to' blocks with the left property values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the correct syntax: @keyframes slide { from { left: 0px; } to { left: 200px; } }

steps.title: Apply the animation to the element
steps.instruction: Add the animation property to your element's CSS rule, specifying the keyframes name and a duration of 2 seconds.
steps.hint: Use the animation property with the format: animation: keyframes-name duration;
steps.expectedOutcome: The element's CSS rule now includes an animation property that references your keyframes with a 2-second duration.
successCriteria: The animation property is added to the element's CSS rule with the correct keyframes name and a duration value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the animation property with both the keyframes name and a duration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation property wasn't properly added. Check that you've included it in the element's CSS rule with the correct syntax.

steps.title: Add animation timing function
steps.instruction: In the CSS rule for your element, add the animation-timing-function property and set it to 'ease-in-out'.
steps.hint: Add animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; inside the element's CSS rule to control the pacing of the animation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The animation will now have a smooth easing effect at the start and end.
successCriteria: The animation-timing-function property is added to the element's CSS rule with the value 'ease-in-out'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the animation-timing-function property with the value 'ease-in-out' inside the element's CSS rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation-timing-function property is missing or incorrect. Add animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; to the element's CSS rule.

steps.title: Set animation iteration count
steps.instruction: Add the animation-iteration-count property to your element's CSS rule to control how many times the animation repeats.
steps.hint: Use the animation-iteration-count property with a numeric value (like 2, 3, or infinite) in the same CSS rule where you applied the animation property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The animation will now repeat a specific number of times instead of running once.
successCriteria: The animation-iteration-count property is added to the element's CSS rule with a valid value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the animation-iteration-count property to the correct CSS rule with a valid value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation-iteration-count property is missing or incorrectly placed. Add it to the same CSS rule where you applied the animation property.

steps.title: Define animation direction
steps.instruction: Add an animation-direction property to your element's CSS rule to control the playback direction of the animation.
steps.hint: Use the animation-direction property with a value like 'normal', 'reverse', 'alternate', or 'alternate-reverse'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The animation-direction property is added to your element's CSS rule, specifying how the animation should play (forward, reverse, or alternate).
successCriteria: The CSS contains an animation-direction property with a valid value in your element's rule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the animation-direction property is correctly added to your element's CSS rule with a valid value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation-direction property is missing or incorrect. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create a multi-step @keyframes animation
steps.instruction: Create a new @keyframes rule named 'multiStep' that defines intermediate states at 0%, 50%, and 100%.
steps.hint: Use @keyframes multiStep { 0% { ... } 50% { ... } 100% { ... } } to create a three-stage animation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new @keyframes rule named 'multiStep' is added with three percentage-based keyframes.
successCriteria: The code contains @keyframes multiStep with 0%, 50%, and 100% blocks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your @keyframes rule is named 'multiStep' and includes 0%, 50%, and 100% blocks.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @keyframes rule is missing or incorrect. Create a new @keyframes rule named 'multiStep' with 0%, 50%, and 100% states.

steps.title: Apply the multi-step animation to a new element
steps.instruction: Create a second div element with class 'animated-box-2' and apply the 'multiStep' animation to it with all animation properties (duration, timing function, iteration count, direction).
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule for .animated-box-2 that includes the animation property with the 'multiStep' keyframes name and all the animation sub-properties you've learned.
steps.expectedOutcome: A second animated element appears on the page with the multi-step animation applied, using all the animation properties you've configured.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .animated-box-2 exists with the animation property that references 'multiStep' and includes duration, timing function, iteration count, and direction values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the second element, but check that you've included all the animation properties (duration, timing function, iteration count, direction) in the animation shorthand.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second element isn't properly animated. Make sure you're applying the 'multiStep' animation to .animated-box-2 with the animation property that includes all the required sub-properties.

steps.title: Add animation delay and fill mode
steps.instruction: Add animation-delay and animation-fill-mode properties to both animation rules in your CSS.
steps.hint: Add animation-delay: 1s; and animation-fill-mode: forwards; to both the original element's animation and the second element's animation.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both animations will have a 1-second delay before starting and will retain the final keyframe styles after completion.
successCriteria: Both CSS rules contain animation-delay: 1s; and animation-fill-mode: forwards; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some animation properties, but make sure both animation rules have both animation-delay: 1s; and animation-fill-mode: forwards; properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required animation-delay and animation-fill-mode properties are missing from one or both animation rules. Review the instruction and try again.
